text:
A: Now then.
B: Hello.
A: Gary. Hucknall, Nottingham way.
B: Tomas. Milton Keynes.
A: What do you do then?
B: Injection moulding. Operator. Plastic packaging, tubs, lids.
A: You're joking. Same. I'm setter-operator, components. Twenty-two year.
B: Twenty-two years. You are setter?
A: Setter, yeah. Do my own changeovers, own settings. I keep a notebook, because the system's never right. You change a tool, you look at what it says on the screen, and it's somebody's guess from six month ago.
B: Yes! Exactly this. I always check myself. Temperature, pressure, cycle time. Other guys just press start and go smoke. Then I come on next shift, everything is scrap.
A: Lowest scrap rate on our line, mine. Every month. There's a new lad keeps putting the cycle times in wrong. I've told him three times.
B: And he is on phone.
A: On his phone. Every one of them. Do you know what I mean.
B: Yeah, yeah. I say to them, put away, watch machine. They don't like me.
A: They don't have to like you. They have to do it right.
B: This is what I think also. I want to be setter, or shift technician. For the money, and less line work. How you get it?
A: Er, I just did it. Time. You know the machines better than the bloke above you, eventually they've got no choice. Get yourself on every changeover you can, make sure the supervisor sees you doing it, and keep your own record so you can show 'em. Don't wait for them to offer, because they won't.
B: Supervisor trusts me with changeovers already. Mm. I will ask.
A: Ask. And make sure the overtime's going to you while you're at it.
B: Ha. I always see overtime first. Best paid shifts, before anybody knows.
A: Good lad. That's how you do it, to be fair.
B: You are on shifts?
A: Permanent days now. Did rotating for years. Earned it. You?
B: Four on, four off. Twelve hours. I don't know what day it is ever.
A: That'll do your head in.
B: Is okay. Four days off, I do other things. I fix bikes, sell on Marketplace.
A: I do fences. Sheds. Weekends, cash, word of mouth. I've got a Skoda Superb estate, you'd be surprised what goes in the back of it.
B: Cash is good. Everything now is expensive. Rent, food. When I come here, rent was half.
A: Diesel. I fill up every other day now, near enough. And they want you to pay more council tax for the same potholes.
B: Yes. And the airport. Luton, eight pounds only to drop off car. Eight pounds for five minutes.
A: Same at East Midlands. Daylight robbery. I book Tenerife a year ahead, get it sorted before they put it up.
B: I also. Four months before, minimum. I compare every day. Only small bag.
A: Never pay for the seats. They sit you together anyway half the time.
B: Exactly. Is a trick.
A: It's all a trick. You've got to watch 'em.
B: Mm. You are first person today who talks sense.
A: Ha. I'll take that.
